sanskrit: bhavyaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyacca sarvaṃ jānaṃti yāṃti ca | paṃcatanmātrarūpaṃ ca manobuddhirahaṃjaḍāḥ || 145 || navatattavamayaṃ dehaṃ daśamaḥ puruṣo mataḥ | tasmādgaṃdhena tṛpyaṃti rasatattvena te tathā || 146 || śabdatattvena tuṣyaṃti sparśatattvaṃ ca gṛhṇate | śuci dṛṣṭvā ta tuṣyaṃti nātra rājanbhavenmṛṣā || 147 ||
english: 145-147. They know the past, the present and the future. They assume the form of subtle elements. Their physical body consists of nine principles, viz. the five Tanmātras (subtle elements of sound etc.), the mind, the intellect, the ego and the Jaḍa (i.e. Prakṛti); Puruṣa is considered to be the tenth one. Therefore, they are satisfied with the subtle essence of smell, taste and sound. They take the essence of touch. They are contented on seeing a pure and clean thing. O king, there is nothing false in this.

english: 12-15. On account of this great sin the king became a Cātaka bird in the course of three births, a vulture in one birth, and a dog in the course of seven births.
